description.narrative: More effective and accountable humanitarian action to improve the lives of people affected by crises. På svenska: Mer effektivt och mer ansvarstagande humanitärt bistånd som förbättrar krisdrabbade människors liv.

Insatsen avser 6 MSEK i kärnstöd under 2021-2023 till The New Humanitarian (TNH) för genomförande av deras mediaverksamhet. The New Humanitarian är en icke-vinstdrivande medieorganisation som bland annat publicerar en digital tidning med nyheter om och från humanitära kriser. Genom ett nätverk av dussintals lokala och internationella korrespondenter mfl erbjuder TNH en unik mediatäckning från humanitära hotspots och knutpunkter i mer än 60 länder. Genom sitt arbete som också omfattar grävande journalistik, kan de humanitära aktörerna i systemet utkrävas ansvar för brister och missförhållanden i verksamheter. TNH: s rapportering uppmärksammar även kriser som hamnat i mediaskugga och deras arbete kan genom att rikta strålkastarljus på humanitära behov som inte tillgodosetts påverka givarströmmar och beslut om finansiering. TNH påverkar inte bara givare utan även beslutsprocesser i länderna där kriserna utspelar sig. TNH är en viktig referenspunkt för det humanitära systemet som bidrar till information, kvalitet och ansvarsutkrävande av humanitära aktörer.

Sida proposes to contribute with 6 million SEK in core support during 2021-2023 to The New Humanitarian for the implementation of their media operations. The New Humanitarian (TNH) is a non-profit media organization that publishes and digital newspaper with news about and from humanitarian crises. Through a network of dozens of local and international correspondents, TNH offers unique media coverage from humanitarian hotspots and hubs in more than 60 countries. Through their work, the humanitarian actors in the system can be held accountable for shortcomings and misconduct in activities. THN's reporting also draws attention to crises that have fallen into the shadow of the media, and their work can, by focusing the spotlight on humanitarian needs that have not been met, influence donor flows and decisions on funding. TNH affects not only donors but also decision-making processes in the countries where the crises take place. TNH is an important reference point for the humanitarian system that contributes to information, quality and accountability of humanitarian actors.

description.narrative:
Overall, TNH has a very relevant role in the sector and beyond in delivering high quality journalism on a broad array of humanitarian issues. Some examples of the success presented for 2024 include:
- Publishing 414 reports - Recognised with 5 awards and nominations - 305 000 social media followers - 335 000 views on Youtube
2024 was the deadliest year on record for aid workers and journalists faced unprecedented threats such as targeted killings and systematic disinformation campaigns. Despite this, TNHs commitments and journalism contributed to shaping localisation debates, exposed sexual abuse by aid workers and peacekeepers, and influenced asylum policies.
The biannual audience survey confirmed that their journalism remained a key catalyst for action across the humanitarian sector with more than 80% of readers claiming that reporting pushed them to explore new topics, while 78% say it drove them to conduct further research or advocacy on certain topics. In addition, readers continued to turn to TNH for expert insights, reinforcing the need for their role in informing, facilitating, and reporting on humanitarian crises across the world.
Throughout the year TNH's reporting has been praised by its audience as an invaluable source of information for humanitarian policy makers and practitioners while ICVA has mentioned TNH's insightful way of reporting on localisation and issues connected thereto. In addition, TNH has been praised particulary for its coverage of issues related to detention of Venezuelans in the United States.
Below follows concrete examples of topics and events covered by TNH in 2024:
- In April TNH investigated Egypt's detention and deportation of Sudanese refugees in collaboration with the Refugees Platform in Egypt. The investigation was cited by the Global Detention Project, used by Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch reports and prompted internal reviews by European awareness. It was also shortlisted for the 2024 Fetisov Award for Outstanding Investigative Reporting. - In December TNH conducted an investigation discussing targeting of aid workers and starvation in northern Gaza. This investigation was submitted as evidence to the ICC and shared with stakeholders in the active genocide case in the ICJ. The investigation was also cited in UK and US parliamentary discussions, translated and published in Arabic and shared across humanitarian networks. - Throughout the year TNH continued to drive accountability on sexual abuse in the aid sector. TNH made an investigation into reports of sexual abuses in the Central African Republic. Something that prompted both MINUSCA and the government to make official responses. In addition, TNH's investigation into the largest sexual abuse scandal in the Democratic Republic of Congo was referenced in a 2024 MOPAN assessment.
Additional situations that were covered by TNH include the worlds fastest growing but most neglected humanitarian crises in Burkina Faso, the unprecedented aid worker death toll in Gaza and the war with Israel, the fast-changing war in Myanmar, Haiti and the Kenya-led police mission, the perilous migrant route along the Darien Gap between Colombia and Panama, the Taliban's policies on women and girls in Afghanistan, the siege and starvation of people in Darfur's El Fasher in Sudan, and the collapse of Bashar al-Assad's regime in Syria.
